      <title>Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda</link>
      <description><p>Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’</p><p>Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.</p><p>The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/26/meps-back-plans-for-return-hubs-raising-fears-of-human-rights-black-holes">newly agreed returns law</a> that allows<em> </em>people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Delaware hit by rare November tornado</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/16/delaware-hit-by-rare-november-tornado</link>
      <description><p>Meanwhile, severe thunderstorms bring hailstones the size of baseballs in Argentina</p><p>The National Weather Service in the US has confirmed that an EF1 tornado touched down south-east of Newark in the Salem Woods neighbourhood, Delaware, on Thursday. The tornado reached 160 metres wide, had a path length of 4.4 miles (7.1km) and reached estimated peak winds of up to 100mph (161km/h). There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95. Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The only other November tornado recorded was in 1989.</p><p>Severe storms have also resulted in tornadoes in Argentina as well as large hailstones. A round of severe thunderstorms moved through the central Córdoba province on Friday, bringing hailstones up to the size of a baseball (about 7.5cm in diameter). Parts of the province recorded up to 73mm of rainfall in just six hours early on Saturday. Such storms are common at this time of year. Water vapour from the Amazon meeting the Andes quickly condenses, resulting in massive cloud formations often associated with heavy downpours, lightning, tornadoes and large hailstones.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/16/delaware-hit-by-rare-november-tornado">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/13/storm-charles-floods-flight-cancellations-southern-europe-weather</link>
      <description><p>Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week </p><p>Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.</p><p>After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/13/storm-charles-floods-flight-cancellations-southern-europe-weather">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Andy Burnham to say Brexit ‘has not worked’ and he will sign new deal with EU</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/16/andy-burnham-brexit-has-not-worked-sign-new-deal-with-eu</link>
      <description><p>PM to meet European leaders at summit this week aiming to secure agreements that ‘could raise GDP by 0.4%’</p><p>Andy Burnham will say on Monday that Brexit “has not worked” and that he will sign a new deal with the EU.</p><p>It is the latest in a string of comments by the prime minister criticising Brexit, after he told the Welsh Labour conference on Saturday that <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/andy-burnham-says-uk-lost-more-than-we-gained-brexit">the UK has “lost more than we gained”</a> through leaving the EU.</p><p>Is consistent with the Labour manifesto and the government’s red lines.</p><p>It improves the Brexit deal and brings it closer to what people thought they were voting for in 2016.</p><p>And it passes the so-called “<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/jun/19/andy-burnham-wins-makerfield-byelection-paving-way-labour-leadership-challenge">Makerfield</a> test” by delivering real, tangible improvements in people’s everyday lives.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/16/andy-burnham-brexit-has-not-worked-sign-new-deal-with-eu">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Monday briefing: The many stages of the UK-EU relationship – and what’s next</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/monday-briefing-the-many-stages-of-the-uk-eu-relationship-and-whats-next</link>
      <description><p>In today’s newsletter: From situationship to a possible makeup, a look at the evolving relationship, and the bloc’s big feelings about the future</p><p>Good morning. Ahead of the hotly anticipated UK-EU summit this Friday, Andy Burnham is expected to make the reset of our relationship with Europe the pivotal theme of his white-tie speech at the lord mayor’s banquet in London tonight.</p><p>The prospect of closer ties – and the possibility of going “all the way” to reversing Brexit – has been met with jubilation and relief in some quarters and vehement opposition in others, while around Westminster and across the media the psychodrama has been spiralling for weeks.</p><p><em><strong>UK news </strong></em>| A woman who alleges she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16 has waived her right to anonymity to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/law/2026/nov/15/uk-government-to-consider-changing-age-of-consent-after-allegations-against-russell-brand">campaign for a staggered age of consent</a>, which would make it illegal for adults over a certain age to have sex with 16- and 17-year-olds.</p><p><em><strong>Youth unemployment </strong></em>| Andy Burnham has pledged to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/15/no-free-lunch-milburn-mcfadden-kuenssberg-uk-benefits-youth-unemployment-neet">intervene as early as childhood </a>to tackle youth unemployment before a watershed review, promising “a root-and-branch rethink of how we support childhood in the modern world”.</p><p><em><strong>Environment </strong></em>| The strongest El Niño in centuries has added urgency to UN climate talks in Turkey as vulnerable countries face “compounding” crises. In other Cop31 news, queer and gay protesters <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/lgbtq-protesters-defy-crackdown-in-turkey-to-march-with-cop31-activists">defied a crackdown</a> on LGBTQ+ rights in Turkey to lead a civil society climate march.</p><p><em><strong>UK news </strong></em>| Two people aged 22 and 23 have died after their car <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/nov/15/leeds-car-pursued-by-police-crashes-into-another-vehicle">was hit by a BMW being pursued by police</a>. West Yorkshire police said four people had been arrested and appealed for witnesses to come forward.</p><p><em><strong>Air transport </strong></em>| The Trump administration says Friday’s four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that delayed or cancelled thousands of flight <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/faa-ground-stop-flights-resume-airport-chaos">stemmed from routine maintenance</a>. The US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/15/transportation-secretary-sean-duffy-faa-flight-stoppag">blamed prior presidents and Congress</a> for the stoppage.</p><p><em><strong>Tuesday </strong></em>| The former health and social care secretary Alan Milburn’s long-awaited review into why increasing numbers of young people are falling out of work and education, is expected to be released.</p><p><em><strong>Thursday</strong></em> | German chancellor Friedrich Merz, French president Emmanuel Macron and UK prime minister Andy Burnham will be among around 20 heads of state meeting in Berlin to discuss defence funding for Ukraine, and to establish a unified position on future peace negotiations in its war with Russia.</p><p><em><strong>Friday</strong></em> | This marks last day of the world’s biggest annual climate conference, Cop31, in Turkey, with final negotiations taking place.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/monday-briefing-the-many-stages-of-the-uk-eu-relationship-and-whats-next">Continue reading...</a></description>

French actor Gérard Depardieu has apologised after withdrawing his appeal against a May 2025 conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">514af00c-e1a1-11f1-82bc-0f0371ba9765</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:19:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French cybercrime unit probes massive cyberattack on La Poste subsidiary</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261116-french-cybercrime-unit-probes-massive-cyberattack-on-la-poste-subsidiary</link><description>
A French anti-cybercrime unit was on Monday investigating a massive cyberattack which targeted a subsidiary of the La Poste group mid-September. The contact details of 22 million people were exposed during the attack, the Paris prosecutor's office confirmed on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f7093a68-e114-11f1-aa3b-e18acb043b04</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 07:01:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg">REUTERS - ERIC GAILLARD</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Harki families take legal action over children's 'ghost graves' in France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261115-harki-families-take-legal-action-over-children-s-ghost-graves-in-france</link><description>
Five families of Harkis – Algerians who fought for the French during Algeria's war of independence – have filed a legal complaint seeking answers over children who died in the 1960s in a former Harki camp in the south of France, and whose remains have since disappeared.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d71114e0-dd33-11f1-ac87-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32476WP.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d71114e0-dd33-11f1-ac87-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32476WP.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cb9c44a8-dded-11f1-9b62-d30335cd8455</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:07:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d71114e0-dd33-11f1-ac87-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32476WP.jpg">© Pascal Guyot / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Women in France report painful periods after exposure to tear gas at protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261115-women-in-france-report-painful-periods-after-exposure-to-tear-gas-at-protests</link><description>
Thousands of women in France have reported unusually painful periods, heavy bleeding and disrupted menstrual cycles after being exposed to tear gas during the country's recent protests, prompting calls for an investigation into its possible effects on reproductive health.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5343e1a8-dd22-11f1-9ec6-3535b33525c6</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:14:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Stephane Mahe</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>How France's student protests grew into a broader movement amid police violence</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261114-how-france-s-student-protests-grew-into-a-broader-movement-amid-police-violence</link><description>
What began in September as a student protest over deteriorating school conditions has over recent weeks grown into a broader social movement across France. The violent police response, notably against young protesters, has helped galvanise support, drawing in university students, trade unions and the wider public.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/7bafaefa-d940-11f1-a471-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151110Z-1962061008-RC2PHOAWS3MA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/7bafaefa-d940-11f1-a471-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151110Z-1962061008-RC2PHOAWS3MA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5254f58-dea5-11f1-81d0-4703a0e08d35</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:11:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/7bafaefa-d940-11f1-a471-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151110Z-1962061008-RC2PHOAWS3MA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© Abdul Saboor/Reuters</source><dc:creator>Sarah Elzas</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fifth wave of French protests to focus on child protection and police laws</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261114-fifth-wave-of-french-protests-to-focus-on-child-protection-and-police-laws</link><description>
France faces more rallies on Saturday with demonstrators venting frustrations ranging from inflation, to child protection measures and opposition to a new police bill.

      <description><p>Sales of built units fell to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, with mortgage rates at nearly three-year high</p><p>US existing home sales hit a 16-year low in October as buyers were driven away by high <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/money/mortgage-rates">mortgage rates</a> and rising inflation, according to new data released on Wednesday.</p><p>Sales of already built units dropped to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, the National Association of Realtors (NAR) reported. The median existing-home sales price increased slightly to $416,700.       <description><p>‘The post-election wish list is about to run into harsh fiscal reality: there is no money’</p><p>Is this an opportunity for a new America?       <description><p>Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected spy is Silicon Valley’s worst nightmare come true</p><p>The resignation this week of Nvidia’s founder and CEO Jensen Huang is one of the most astonishing corporate scandals in memory, featuring allegations of international espionage and extramarital affairs involving one of the world’s most powerful men.       <title>Farewell to Elon Musk’s Cybertruck. Has any car ever been more repellent? | Arwa Mahdawi</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent</link>
      <description><p>Safety campaigners have condemned it and owners have complained about it. Goodbye to a steel monstrosity seemingly designed by a five-year-old</p><p>Elon Musk is having a rough go of it, isn’t he? The world’s richest man spent almost half a billion dollars on the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/04/elon-musk-midterm-spending-analysis">midterms</a> in a failed attempt to defend Republican control of government. Now the tech mogul, who moved from California to Texas to escape Democrats and regulations, finds himself in a newly blue state. He also finds himself the subject of an unflattering <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/08/musk-review-epic-study-worlds-richest-most-banal-man-elon-film">documentary</a> and, if the Democrats follow through on threats to investigate him, could potentially be in a spot of legal bother.</p><p>And to top it all off? Musk’s beloved Cybertruck, the steel monstrosity that looks as if it were designed by a five-year-old, is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/06/tesla-to-wind-down-cybertruck-production-as-elon-musk-focuses-on-robotics-and-ai">winding down production</a>. According to Musk, this isn’t because it’s an abject failure, but because he is channelling his energy into other things. “This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media,” Musk <a href="https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2119691615774146614?a=pN3ISFVZZ-aU4_-TlJw&amp;s=20">tweeted</a> on Monday. “But rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.” (The Cybercab is a two-passenger robotaxi.)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>A layoff and a leap of faith convinced Katie Teixeira she had what it takes to run her own business</p><p>In 2010, Katie Teixeira adopted a kitten found all alone in an abandoned house. Frank, out of work since being <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/feb/11/thomas-frank-sacked-tottenham-head-coach">dismissed by Tottenham</a> in February, was quickly identified as Palace’s main target and has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal at the Premier League’s bottom club.</p><p>Frank spoke to Palace in the summer about succeeding Oliver Glasner but decided he was not ready to return to the dugout because he wanted to take a break from football.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/thomas-frank-confirmed-crystal-palace-manager-pierre-sage">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Mauricio Pochettino sends coaches to Manchester to help prepare for United job</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/mauricio-pochettino-assistants-manchester-united-usmnt</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Assistant Jesús Pérez and two others depart US early</p></li><li><p>Pochettino to begin as United head coach on Wednesday</p></li></ul><p>Mauricio Pochettino has sent key members of his coaching staff to England in an early move to prepare for his <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/mauricio-pochettino-confirmed-manchester-united-usa">role as Manchester United’s new head coach</a> while he gets set to lead the US men’s national team for a final time.</p><p>Pochettino’s assistant Jesús Pérez, goalkeeping coach Toni Jiménez and athletic coach Sebastiano Pochettino travelled to Manchester soon after the US’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/usmnt-haiti-pulisic-pochettino-nations-league-quarter-final">6-0 victory over Haiti in Miami</a> and in the run-up to United’s Premier League visit to Liverpool on Sunday, when Pochettino will take charge of a fourth English team for a first time.       <title>Spain in pain as historic run ends but De la Fuente feels best is yet to come</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/luis-de-la-fuente-spain-england-nations-league</link>
      <description><p>While the head coach, players and Spanish press were magnanimous in defeat, there was pride mixed in with disappointment – and confidence the future is still bright</p><p>“With every game, defeat gets closer,” Luis de la Fuente had said and on Sunday night it finally came. Spain had lost only one competitive game since Scotland in March 2023 back when <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/jul/14/how-low-profile-bull-fight-fan-luis-de-la-fuente-won-over-sceptical-spain">the coach hadn’t won anything</a> and didn’t look like he ever would – and that solitary loss was on penalties in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/jun/08/portugal-sink-spain-in-penalty-shootout-to-win-nations-league-crown">2025 Nations League final</a>. Statistically, they said, penalties don’t count, so while Portugal lifted the trophy that night, the team that won the European Championship and World Cup in the summers either side also claimed a Fifa record of 44 official games unbeaten. <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/spain-england-nations-league-match-report">And then England turned up at the Metropolitano</a>.</p><p>A night that started with Iker Casillas, Fernando Torres and Fernando Llorente handing the World Cup to Unai Simón ended with Spain trying to overhaul a shock 3-0 deficit. Against 10 men and led by a superb Lamine Yamal, Spain made De la Fuente think for a while that they would, but it wasn’t to be.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/luis-de-la-fuente-spain-england-nations-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><ul><li><p>Diallo confirmed by Uefa as its chosen candidate</p></li><li><p>He accused Infantino of seriously damaging football</p></li></ul><p>The French Football Federation president, Philippe Diallo, has been confirmed as Uefa’s surprise late choice to run for the Fifa presidency.       <title>Football Daily | England’s Nations League triumph in Spain sparks familiar rush to glory</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/england-spain-nations-league-victory-football-daily-newsletter</link>
      <description><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/info/2022/nov/14/football-daily-email-sign-up"><strong>Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!</strong></a></p><p>Glory. Imminent and near-enough-guaranteed glory. That, surely, is what we’re looking at from the giddy heights England reached <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/spain-england-nations-league-match-report">in crushing Spain 3-2 on Sunday</a>. “If we can find that first hour consistently, we are a genuine favourites for the next tournament,” roared Steven Gerrard, a statement he believed in so much he then said it again using different words: “The first 60 minutes told me, from watching it, that we’re capable of winning the next tournament. That’s the big thing to take away.” Thomas Tuchel reckoned England had reached the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/thomas-tuchel-england-spain-nations-league">“highest level football-wise in all aspects of the game”</a>. This is the kind of positivity engendered in visiting international teams when they romp to victory in Madrid. Just listen to what the England captain said on the flight home: “You play like that and you’ve got a chance against anyone, anywhere. You get 11 fellows who can play a bit – and let’s face it, they’re not going to be there in the first place if they can’t – and you get them running themselves off their feet, working themselves into the ground for an hour and a half, and you’re odds on before you start, aren’t you.”</p><p>Did anyone else notice that Saturday evening’s match between Fleetwood Town and Tranmere Rovers involved two teams with a 100% record against Arsenal? Town a few weeks ago and the mighty Rovers way back in 1973. Both in the League Cup – or whatever it’s called nowadays” – Jim Salter.</p><p>So Mauricio Pochettino bursts out crying when announcing his job at Manchester United (<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/pierre-sage-crystal-palace-football-daily-newsletter">Friday’s Quote of the Day</a>). Assuming the move goes to plan, he might as well get the practice as no doubt, tears will flow again before too long” – Nigel Sanders.</p><p>Re: Haitian security forces regaining control of the national stadium (Friday’s News, Bits and Bobs, full email edition). Never mind the army, why are there trees <em>inside</em> the stadium? How many Tonda Eckerts does the Haitian league have?” – Yannick Woudstra [watch out for <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/gallery/2019/sep/06/for-forest-an-art-intervention-transforming-austrian-stadium">this one</a>, then – Football Daily Ed].</p><p><em><strong>This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version,<a href="https://preview.gutools.co.uk/info/2016/jan/05/the-fiver-email-sign-up"> </a><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/info/2022/nov/14/football-daily-email-sign-up">just visit this page and follow the instructions</a>.</strong></em> </p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/england-spain-nations-league-victory-football-daily-newsletter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/wsl-talking-points-chelseas-gamble-pays-off-and-have-arsenal-lost-fear-factor</link>
      <description><p>Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw</p><p>Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. <strong>Suzanne Wrack</strong></p><p><em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/chelsea-manchester-city-womens-super-league-match-report">Match report: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City</a></em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/wsl-talking-points-chelseas-gamble-pays-off-and-have-arsenal-lost-fear-factor">Continue reading...</a></description>

up for our free newsletter here</strong></a></p></li></ul><p><em>Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager?</em> <strong>– Tom S</strong></p><p>Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling.</p><p><em>This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/jul/20/sign-up-for-soccer-with-jonathan-wilson-his-free-weekly-newsletter-on-european-soccer?utm_term=68ff7d8f6c73dffc08f382888be1de2a&amp;amp;utm_campaign=SoccerwithJonathanWilson&amp;amp;utm_source=esp&amp;amp;utm_medium=Email&amp;amp;CMP=soccerwithjonathanwilson_email">Subscribe for free here</a>.       <description><p>Brazilian legend, an investor at Serie C club, showed glimpses of old brilliance as he played 45 minutes for the promotion-chasing side</p><p>It may have been the longest buildup in world football. In June, the former Barcelona and Brazil legend <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/24/ronaldinho-ravenna-serie-c-age-46">Ronaldinho was unveiled by the Serie C side Ravenna</a> to make his comeback at the age of 46 – 11 years after his last official game.       <description><p>Problems faced by Gotham FC and Washington Spirit over staging of their playoff semi-finals shows the league still has work to do</p><p>In so many ways, Icahn Stadium, tucked away on Randall’s Island in the Harlem River, is a fantastic place to watch soccer.</p><p>The 5,000-seat facility was thrown together in the early 2000s, constructed to replace Downing Stadium, an aging relic that hosted Pelé’s first match with the New York Cosmos 51 years ago.       <description><p>Hopes of promotion remain alive, but another costly collapse has raised familiar questions before the decisive Nations League game with Kosovo</p><p>The Republic of Ireland stand on the verge, although of what, nobody seems quite sure. Tuesday’s final Nations League group match, at home to Kosovo, presents a chance for progress or yet another opportunity to showcase a frustrating habit of messing things up.</p><p>For 78 minutes in Linz on Saturday, Heimir Hallgrímsson’s side gave as good as they got against an Austria side who had not lost at home for a little more than three years. Set up in a compact, attack-minded formation they carried credible threat against hosts managed by Ralf Rangnick, but to nobody’s great surprise Sasa Kalajdzic broke the deadlock, scrambling home the winner from a needlessly conceded and poorly defended corner.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/republic-of-ireland-heimir-hallgrimsson-nations-league-kosovo">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Three Lions’ win over Spain comes in two acts: the first superb, the second heroic | Sid Lowe</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/england-superb-heroic-spain-nations-league</link>
      <description><p>Visitors take game to world champions and, though their hold on possession plummets, their rearguard is outstanding</p><p>In the final, absurdly tense moments before <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/spain-england-nations-league-match-report">England finally did it</a> and Spain finally fell, when Dan Burn had been sent on to do Dan Burn things, when the board had gone up with a 4 on but the clock wasn’t moving fast enough and the men in red kept coming back, Harry Kane had come to the side of the pitch to stand beside Thomas Tuchel. Palms out, Kane signalled and directed and appealed with his teammates to hold on to what they had: <em>s</em><em>omehow, anyhow</em>. What they had was special, but their grip on it was not as secure as it had seemed. Not as secure as it should have been too.</p><p>Tuchel gave Kane a nudge that looked pretty playful considering the pressure, before Marc Bollengier, the fourth official, ordered him back to the bench. But England’s captain was not gone for long and when he returned he was joined by almost all of them, awaiting the big moment. From there, he watched James Trafford make an astonishing double save, a moment of heroism that allowed them to hang on. Then, standing alongside the rest who could no longer just sit there, he saw the last header clear – Dan Burn things – before the whistle went. Then he and they went on one last run, back on to the pitch.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/england-superb-heroic-spain-nations-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Terry Butcher: ‘I’ve learned to live with the Hand of God goal better’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/terry-butcher-ive-learned-to-live-with-the-hand-of-god-goal-better</link>
      <description><p>The former England centre-back answers your questions on Diego Maradona, Bobby Robson and on staying in strange places</p><p>“Have you made up all these on your own?” asks Terry Butcher, sitting in a London office in the week he is presented with his England legacy cap. It turns out dozens of Guardian readers want to pick the brains of a much-loved centre-back who was feted en route to a World Cup semi-final and tormented four years previously by the mercurial genius of Diego Maradona.</p><p>Did Maradona ever admit to the “Hand of God”? Butcher found himself in the post-match doping-control room alongside his nemesis at the Azteca in 1986. “I tapped my head, then my hand, and then he tapped his head,” Butcher says. “He didn’t admit to it because, if he had, I’d have been right across that room.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/terry-butcher-ive-learned-to-live-with-the-hand-of-god-goal-better">Continue reading...</a></description>

French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

Le Ghana et la Guinée terminent cette série de matches de qualifications pour la CAN 2027 dans une meilleure position grâce à des victoires contre la Somalie et l'Érythrée. Quant au Bénin, il a déjà un pied en Afrique de l'Est et pourrait être qualifié par le résultat de Mauritanie - Burkina Faso mardi.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/642d4f22-e1e6-11f1-95d4-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/000-A69Z882.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/642d4f22-e1e6-11f1-95d4-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/000-A69Z882.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">14e4a762-e1e6-11f1-ac94-07600c859831</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 18:01:12 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/642d4f22-e1e6-11f1-95d4-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/000-A69Z882.jpg">© Thomas Kienzle, AFP</source><dc:creator>Romain HOUEIX</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>La primaire de la droite, "un aveu d’échec" pour Gabriel Attal et Bruno Retailleau</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261116-france-presidentielle-2027-primaire-de-la-droite-un-aveu-dechec-pour-gabriel-attal-et-bruno-retailleau</link><description>
Après y avoir longtemps été opposés, Gabriel Attal et Bruno Retailleau appellent désormais de leurs vœux à l’organisation d’une primaire pour désigner un candidat unique de la droite et du centre. L'objectif : éviter un second tour de la présidentielle opposant Marine Le Pen et Jean-Luc Mélenchon. Un revirement qui coïncide avec leur chute conjointe dans les sondages.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6c364b1c-e1da-11f1-a9d7-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/main-primaire-candidats.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6c364b1c-e1da-11f1-a9d7-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/main-primaire-candidats.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">398f6e36-e1d1-11f1-ac4e-af1d6fdd21cf</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:57:20 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6c364b1c-e1da-11f1-a9d7-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/main-primaire-candidats.png">© AFP / Studio graphique, FMM</source><dc:creator>Romain BRUNET</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>JOJ Dakar 2026 : une première olympique réussie pour l'Afrique</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-joj-dakar-2026-une-premi%C3%A8re-olympique-r%C3%A9ussie-pour-l-afrique</link><description>
🇸🇳 Les Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse Dakar 2026 s'achèvent sur une performance historique pour l'Afrique : cinq pays africains figurent dans le top 10 du classement des médailles. Athlètes et encadreurs saluent l'organisation de cette première édition olympique sur le continent. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/db3a3f84-e1d3-11f1-807e-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/Couv-Bilan-JOJ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/db3a3f84-e1d3-11f1-807e-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/Couv-Bilan-JOJ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0785227a-e1d4-11f1-be3b-9be425d63698</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:49:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Questions directes</category><title>La Francophonie en crise ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/questions-directes/20261116-la-francophonie-en-crise</link><description>
L’élection du secrétaire général de l’OIF a été reportée d’un an, sur fond de tensions entre la RDC et le Rwanda. Une première pour l’institution, qui interroge sur son avenir. Quel poids la Francophonie peut-elle encore peser sur la scène internationale et comment renforcer la place du français dans le monde ?
 
Christine Desouches, spécialiste de la Francophonie et autrice de De la francophonie, décrypte les enjeux de cette crise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ba893630-e1e4-11f1-9b3b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-181753-182818-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ba893630-e1e4-11f1-9b3b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-181753-182818-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f74bcb9a-e1e5-11f1-9731-915f00d2a277</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:49:17 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Stéphanie ANTOINE</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Triple narchomicide à Marseille en 2020 : deux accusés condamnés à la perpétuité</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261116-triple-narchomicide-%C3%A0-marseille-en-2020-deux-accus%C3%A9s-condamn%C3%A9s-%C3%A0-la-perp%C3%A9tuit%C3%A9</link><description>
Deux figures du narcobanditisme marseillais jugées pour un triple assassinat ont été condamnées, lundi, à des peines de prison à perpétuité assorties d'une période de sûreté. L'une des victimes est le frère aîné du militant antitrafic Amine Kessaci.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/acb179f6-e1de-11f1-9788-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QP7ZQ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/acb179f6-e1de-11f1-9788-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QP7ZQ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">902a148a-e1e0-11f1-8092-f38a56165042</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:23:12 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/acb179f6-e1de-11f1-9788-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QP7ZQ.jpg">© Benoît Peyrucq, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>L'Estonie ferme sa frontière avec la Russie</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-l-estonie-ferme-sa-fronti%C3%A8re-avec-la-russie</link><description>
Dimanche, l'Estonie a annoncé la fermeture de "tous les points de passage à la frontière estono-russe à compter du 1er décembre", après avoir déjoué une tentative d'incendie d'une usine de drones orchestrée, selon ce pays balte, par le renseignement militaire russe, le GRU. Une décision vivement critiquée par le Kremlin lundi.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f1d4f116-e1de-11f1-afdb-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/minia-Estonie-Russie.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f1d4f116-e1de-11f1-afdb-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/minia-Estonie-Russie.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">73eed5dc-e1de-11f1-bc23-39f7c80039f3</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:00:28 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>APEC 2026 : Vers un sommet Xi-Trump-Poutine</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-apec-2026-vers-un-sommet-xi-trump-poutine</link><description>
C’est une première depuis qu’ils sont au pouvoir. Xi Jinping, Vladimir Poutine et Donald Trump tiendront cette semaine une réunion tripartite en marge du sommet de l’Apec en Chine. Volodymyr Zelensky redoute des discussions sur l’Ukraine, dans le dos de Kiev. Mais selon la diplomatie américaine, il sera surtout question de dénucléarisation.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef507dc6-e1dd-11f1-b597-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/minia-baptiste.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef507dc6-e1dd-11f1-b597-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/minia-baptiste.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">077cb59e-e1da-11f1-8427-cd75c91fbb61</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:53:30 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>À l'Affiche !</category><title>Le rappeur sénégalais Samba Peuzzi, nouvelle étoile du hip-hop</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/%C3%A0-l-affiche/20261116-le-rappeur-s%C3%A9n%C3%A9galais-samba-peuzzi-nouvelle-%C3%A9toile-du-hip-hop</link><description>
Dans cette nouvelle édition d'"À l'Affiche", rencontre avec la nouvelle star du hip-hop, le Sénégalais Samba Peuzzi dont le troisième album, "Culture", est sorti en janvier, mêlant rap et afropop. Il est en concert à Montréal vendredi 20 novembre. Ensuite, direction Abidjan pour comprendre comment l'œuvre du photographe Paul Kodjo a été préservée. Enfin, le portrait de Papy Kaluw, un couturier congolais basé au Cap, en Afrique du Sud.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/04089ff8-e1cc-11f1-bcc1-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/CULTURE-16-11-2026-11-00-ING26-CLEAN-A-frame-143061.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/04089ff8-e1cc-11f1-bcc1-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/CULTURE-16-11-2026-11-00-ING26-CLEAN-A-frame-143061.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ac9d508c-e1b3-11f1-bf75-5158cfd5d7ef</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:42:48 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sonia PATRICELLI</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>L'acteur britannique Robert Pattinson devient le nouveau James Bond</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-l-acteur-britannique-robert-pattinson-devient-le-nouveau-james-bond</link><description>
L'acteur britannique Robert Pattinson a été choisi pour incarner James Bond, endossant ainsi le rôle très convoité de l'espion le plus célèbre du monde. Robert Pattinson, qui s'est fait connaître dans le monde entier pour son rôle dans la saga "Twilight" avant de bâtir une carrière éclectique, succède à Daniel Craig, qui a incarné 007 pendant 15 ans.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a9379d08-e1db-11f1-b15b-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/minia-james-bond.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a9379d08-e1db-11f1-b15b-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/minia-james-bond.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">3fcd1c9e-e1db-11f1-86eb-17eb87f97227</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:39:03 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Tibet : quelle succession pour le Dalaï-Lama, le chef spirituel des Tibétains ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-tibet-quelle-succession-pour-le-dala%C3%AF-lama-le-chef-spirituel-des-tib%C3%A9tains</link><description>
Le chef spirituel des Tibétains, âgé de 91 ans, est en exil en Inde depuis 67 ans et se pose, plus que jamais, la question de sa succession ou, plutôt, de sa réincarnation. Un sujet très sensible pour les autorités chinoises. Les précisions de Baptise Fallevoz, correspondant France 24 à Pékin.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/51d57040-e1da-11f1-801a-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-163306-163723-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/51d57040-e1da-11f1-801a-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-163306-163723-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">571a5b7e-e1da-11f1-9f74-8152aa20cf46</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:38:16 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>États-Unis : la célèbre militante écologiste Erin Brockovich défie les géants de la tech</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-%C3%A9tats-unis-la-c%C3%A9l%C3%A8bre-militante-%C3%A9cologiste-erin-brockovich-d%C3%A9fie-les-g%C3%A9ants-de-la-tech</link><description>
L’activiste écologiste Erin Brockovich a fait de la lutte contre les ravages environnementaux des data centers liés à l'intelligence artificielle son nouveau combat. La militante a notamment lancé une Brockovich AI Data Center Reporting pour recenser les projets et alerter sur leur impact. Les précisions de Matthieu Mabin, correspondant France 24 à Washington.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b851e61a-e1d9-11f1-83f7-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-161804-162432-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b851e61a-e1d9-11f1-83f7-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-161804-162432-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bdf103c6-e1d9-11f1-95ec-591890868b6b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:35:18 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Culture</category><title>Nouveau James Bond : l'acteur britannique Robert Pattinson enfile le costume de 007</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/culture/20261116-nouveau-james-bond-acteur-britannique-robert-pattinson-enfile-costume-007</link><description>
L'acteur britannique Robert Pattinson a été choisi pour incarner le personnage de James Bond dans le prochain épisode des aventures de l'espion le plus célèbre du monde, produit pour la première fois par le studio Amazon MGM.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/56be3f90-e1d2-11f1-92c9-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C7FC3U6.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/56be3f90-e1d2-11f1-92c9-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C7FC3U6.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ddec4c0c-e1d5-11f1-b822-7d5303f8a764</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:06:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/56be3f90-e1d2-11f1-92c9-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C7FC3U6.jpg">© Tiziana Fabi, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Triple narchomicide en France : l'heure du verdict pour la DZ Mafia</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-triple-narchomicide-en-france-l-heure-du-verdict-pour-la-dz-mafia</link><description>
Les cinq accusés ont tour à tour présenté leurs "condoléances" aux familles des victimes lundi 16 novembre, sous le regard notamment d'Amine Kessaci et de sa mère, Ouassila, qui portait un pull blanc orné du portrait de son fils cadet Mehdi, lui aussi assassiné. Ce jeune homme de 20 ans, étranger au narcotrafic, a été abattu en plein jour à Marseille il y a un an, en novembre 2025. Le verdict du procès pour triple narchomicide est attendu dans la journée.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/97d75578-e1cf-11f1-828f-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-151542-151730-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/97d75578-e1cf-11f1-828f-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-151542-151730-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9d3cab44-e1cf-11f1-bfe7-4501db9e6a0a</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:06:48 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Procès Depardieu : "je croyais mes gestes sans conséquence, ils ne l'étaient pas"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-proc%C3%A8s-depardieu-je-croyais-mes-gestes-sans-cons%C3%A9quences-ils-ne-l-%C3%A9taient-pas</link><description>
Reconnaissant que ses propos et "certains de (ses) gestes" n'étaient pas "sans conséquence", "particulièrement de la part d'un personnage puissant tel que j'ai pu l'être", admet Gérard Depardieu, condamné à 18 mois de prison avec sursis. L'acteur âgé de 77 ans, a été reconnu coupable d'avoir agressé sexuellement Amélie, une décoratrice, et Sarah (prénom modifié), une assistante réalisatrice sur le film de Jean Becker sorti en 2022.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b253f00e-e1d0-11f1-9c7e-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-151753-151958-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b253f00e-e1d0-11f1-9c7e-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-151753-151958-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b815e510-e1d0-11f1-ba52-697d1920ec3e</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:04:36 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Yémen : le siège du gouvernement menacé par les rebelles Houthis ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-y%C3%A9men-le-si%C3%A8ge-du-gouvernement-menac%C3%A9-par-les-rebelles-houthis</link><description>
Les Houthis sont désormais stationnés dimanche 15 novembre dans le camp d'al-Kharaz, à al-Madharibah, à 60 km de cette importante ville côtière où le gouvernement, internationalement reconnu, s'est replié après avoir perdu, en 2014, la capitale Sanaa et de grands pans du nord du pays, les plus peuplés. Les explications de Karim Sader, politologue et consultant spécialiste des pays du Golfe.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5c6c9544-e1ce-11f1-8736-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-150745-151519-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5c6c9544-e1ce-11f1-8736-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-150745-151519-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61fc92c0-e1ce-11f1-81fe-1db0a2be4f3f</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:58:48 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><title>🔴 Le Français Philippe Diallo candidat à la présidence de la Fifa contre Infantino</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/sports/20261116-presidence-fifa-philippe-diallo-candidat-contre-infantino</link><description></description><guid isPermaLink="false">15725bd0-e1d6-11f1-9e3b-0f3dbdbeb1d6</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:55:35 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>France : Depardieu condamné pour agressions sexuelles, les victimes soulagées mais perplexes</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-france-depardieu-condamn%C3%A9-pour-agressions-sexuelles-les-victimes-soulag%C3%A9es-mais-perplexes</link><description>
Gérard Depardieu a renoncé, lundi 16 novembre, à son procès en appel pour agressions sexuelles lors du tournage du film "Les Volets verts", présentant des "excuses profondes et sincères" aux plaignantes et rendant définitive sa peine de 18 mois de prison avec sursis. La fin d'une ère d'omerta pour les victimes qui restent perplexes : "j'aurais aimé que les excuses arrivent plus tôt (...) ça aurait été mieux qu'il soit là" déclare Amélie, une des deux victimes ayant remporté le procès.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f2ed8110-e1cc-11f1-bee2-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-143002-143845-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f2ed8110-e1cc-11f1-bee2-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-143002-143845-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f83e815a-e1cc-11f1-a723-fb9428fb00c4</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:55:12 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Sports</category><title>Présidence de la Fifa : le Français Philippe Diallo candidat contre Infantino</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/sports/20261116-presidence-fifa-philippe-diallo-candidat-contre-infantino</link><description>
Le président de la Fédération française de football (FFF), Philippe Diallo, est soutenu par l'UEFA pour briguer la présidence de la Fifa le 18 mars prochain. L'instance européenne est en conflit ouvert avec l'actuel président, Gianni Infantino.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b960904e-ace9-11f1-91ec-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B7XH3KH.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b960904e-ace9-11f1-91ec-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B7XH3KH.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d265d466-e1d5-11f1-84ad-f7db50ffbd34</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:54:36 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b960904e-ace9-11f1-91ec-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B7XH3KH.jpg">AFP - FRANCK FIFE</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Guerre hybride : l'Estonie verrouille sa frontière, une réponse efficace à la menace russe ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/europe/20261116-guerre-hybride-l-estonie-verrouille-sa-fronti%C3%A8re-une-r%C3%A9ponse-efficace-%C3%A0-la-menace-russe</link><description>
L’Estonie a annoncé, dimanche, la fermeture de sa frontière avec la Russie après avoir accusé cette dernière d’avoir orchestré une tentative de sabotage d’une usine de drones. Mais à l’heure d’Internet, les agents russes peuvent ignorer les frontières pour mener leur guerre hybride contre les pays européens.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/638675fe-e1d1-11f1-97ac-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/russie-estonie-frontiere.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/638675fe-e1d1-11f1-97ac-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/russie-estonie-frontiere.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b320a8da-e1ce-11f1-b6d1-e3d75fb7560d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:48:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/638675fe-e1d1-11f1-97ac-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/russie-estonie-frontiere.png">© Studio graphique France Médias Monde</source><dc:creator>Sébastian SEIBT</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Riposte ukrainienne : l'unique laison entre la Russie et la péninsule interrompue</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-riposte-ukrainienne-l-unique-laison-entre-la-russie-et-la-p%C3%A9ninsule-interrompue</link><description>
L'Ukraine, qui a frappé le pont reliant la Russie à la Crimée et pris pour cible des raffineries de pétrole, a mené, lundi 16 novembre, sa plus grande attaque nocturne de drones contre la Russie depuis le début de la guerre à grande échelle déclenchée par Moscou en 2022, montrent les données du ministère russe de la Défense. Axe stratégique, le pont de Crimée sert de pont ferroviaire et de pont routier et a d'ailleurs déjà été visé par plusieurs attaques ukrainiennes depuis le début du conflit.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/60ad1fb2-e1cd-11f1-bf78-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-150205-150334-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/60ad1fb2-e1cd-11f1-bf78-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-150205-150334-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">66a29582-e1cd-11f1-9a44-b1af49f76d84</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:47:32 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Amérique du Sud : le pape Léon XIV met fin à sa tournée de 12 jours</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-am%C3%A9rique-du-sud-le-pape-l%C3%A9on-xiv-met-fin-%C3%A0-sa-tourn%C3%A9e-de-12-jours</link><description>
Le pape Léon XIV achève, lundi 16 novembre, une tournée de douze jours en Amérique du Sud, un retour aux sources qui a levé les doutes sur sa convalescence après une opération d'un cancer. À 71 ans, le premier pape américain a parcouru l'Uruguay, l'Argentine et le Pérou, dont il possède aussi la nationalité.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/aafe49f0-e1c9-11f1-a0f0-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-135103-135234-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/aafe49f0-e1c9-11f1-a0f0-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-135103-135234-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b0a0aace-e1c9-11f1-bfa2-e35ab2779ef1</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:40:39 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Ligue des nations : les Bleus qualifiés pour les quarts malgré une prestation mitigée</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-ligue-des-nations-les-bleus-qualifi%C3%A9s-pour-les-quarts-malgr%C3%A9-une-prestation-mitig%C3%A9e</link><description>
L'équipe de France s'est qualifiée dimanche 15 novembre pour les ⁠quarts de finale ​de la Ligue des nations à la suite de sa victoire contre la Turquie (2-1), au stade Atlantique de Bordeaux, malgré une prestation mitigée. Trois jours après le premier revers de ​l'ère Zinédine Zidane, en Italie (3-1), les Bleus ont su réagir, faisant mieux que le nul suffisant pour se qualifier. Les explications de Benoit Perrochais, chroniqueur sport à France 24.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4dad0fdc-e1cb-11f1-b410-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-141640-142251-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4dad0fdc-e1cb-11f1-b410-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-141640-142251-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">53500b2e-e1cb-11f1-a1d5-7394b3f6fc42</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:38:11 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Un "vortex polaire" inédit en Europe : la précocité de ces vents violents inquiète</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-un-vortex-polaire-in%C3%A9dit-en-europe-la-pr%C3%A9cocit%C3%A9-de-ces-vents-violents-inqui%C3%A8te</link><description>
Effet direct du dérèglement climatique : après les canicules de l'été passé, l'hémisphère nord, et notamment l'Europe, pourraient connaître un hiver extrêmement rigoureux. En cause : la désorganisation du vortex polaire. Une perturbation exceptionnellement précoce qui augmente le risque de vagues de froid.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1a2721c6-e1ca-11f1-8192-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-135257-135426-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1a2721c6-e1ca-11f1-8192-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-135257-135426-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1f71ddba-e1ca-11f1-9de9-a98c7ea339d5</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:34:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Immigration aux Canaries : des arrivées en nombre sur l'île d'El Hierro</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-immigration-aux-canaries-des-arriv%C3%A9es-en-nombre-sur-l-%C3%AEle-d-el-hierro</link><description>
Au cours des dix premiers jours du mois de novembre, près de 6 000 clandestins sont arrivés aux Canaries, pour l’essentiel sur l’île d’El Hierro, qui compte 12 000 habitants. Un afflux qui s’explique en partie par la fermeture d’autres voies migratoires. Sur place, les autorités déplorent le manque de ressources humaines et matérielles pour faire face et en appellent à une réponse de l’État.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f76e4b2e-e1c8-11f1-af86-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-134716-134859-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f76e4b2e-e1c8-11f1-af86-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-134716-134859-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fcc7af84-e1c8-11f1-b1bd-7394b3f6fc42</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:32:32 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title>France : News et actualité en continu - France 24</title><description>France 24  couvre les évènements en France et en Outre-mer : politique, culture, faits de société, énergie, crise sociale, sport, santé, avec ses reportages, enquêtes, débats et analyses.</description><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 18:10:43 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/fr/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>La primaire de la droite, "un aveu d’échec" pour Gabriel Attal et Bruno Retailleau</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261116-france-presidentielle-2027-primaire-de-la-droite-un-aveu-dechec-pour-gabriel-attal-et-bruno-retailleau</link><description>
Après y avoir longtemps été opposés, Gabriel Attal et Bruno Retailleau appellent désormais de leurs vœux à l’organisation d’une primaire pour désigner un candidat unique de la droite et du centre. L'objectif : éviter un second tour de la présidentielle opposant Marine Le Pen et Jean-Luc Mélenchon. Un revirement qui coïncide avec leur chute conjointe dans les sondages.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/39cdf0b8-d9d2-11f1-ac00-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/VIGNETTE-Philippe-Aghion0.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/39cdf0b8-d9d2-11f1-ac00-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/VIGNETTE-Philippe-Aghion0.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">3a406cd2-d9ec-11f1-849e-57277d33a762</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 15:50:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Judith GRIMALDI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Teddy Riner réfute être macroniste et qualifie de "baiser empoisonné" les félicitations de Macron</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261114-teddy-riner-r%C3%A9fute-%C3%AAtre-macroniste-qualifie-baiser-empoisonn%C3%A9-f%C3%A9licitations-macron</link><description>
Le judoka et désormais candidat à la présidentielle Teddy Riner s'est défendu samedi d'être macroniste, lors de son déplacement au salon du "Made in France". Le sportif de haut niveau a, en outre, qualifié de "baiser empoisonné" les félicitations d'Emmanuel Macron.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6b1d08ee-e039-11f1-b3ec-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-13T141058Z-238804417-RC20NOAI3PJP-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-RINER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6b1d08ee-e039-11f1-b3ec-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-13T141058Z-238804417-RC20NOAI3PJP-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-RINER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">33616c6c-e03c-11f1-899e-2fc136140861</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 15:12:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6b1d08ee-e039-11f1-b3ec-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-13T141058Z-238804417-RC20NOAI3PJP-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-RINER.jpg">© Gonzalo Fuente, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>"Je ne pensais quand même pas avoir un père nazi" : Edith Pagot, née dans un Lebensborn</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261114-lebensborn-pouponniere-nazie-allemagne-enfants-seconde-guerre-mondiale-edith</link><description>
Il y a 80 ans, en 1946, deux convois d'enfants, dont certains nés dans un Lebensborn, une pouponnière nazie, étaient accueillis à Commercy, dans la Meuse, en provenance d'Allemagne. Parmi eux se trouvait Edith Pagot. Jusqu'à aujourd'hui, cette femme adoptée ignorait qu'elle était née dans un Lebensborn. Elle ne l'a appris que cette année, après des recherches entreprises par sa fille.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9490f12c-c0c2-11f1-985b-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/main-lebensborn.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9490f12c-c0c2-11f1-985b-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/main-lebensborn.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8761c200-c0c3-11f1-8ef6-f76e46373e98</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 12:57:53 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9490f12c-c0c2-11f1-985b-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/main-lebensborn.png">© Studio graphique FMM</source><dc:creator>Stéphanie TROUILLARD</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Acte V de la colère sociale : une mobilisation en baisse, des incidents dans plusieurs villes</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261114-manifestations-du-14-novembre-en-direct-des-revendications-diverses-en-amont-de-l-acte-v</link><description>
Quelque 106 000 personnes ont manifesté samedi en France, dont 24 000 à Paris, lors de l'acte V du mouvement social, a annoncé samedi après-midi le ministère de l'Intérieur. Une mobilisation inférieure à la semaine dernière, qui avait réuni 146 000 personnes, dont 46 000 dans la capitale selon cette même source. La place Beauvau a toutefois souligné ​que la situation a été globalement ​maîtrisée en dépit d'incidents dans plusieurs villes. Retrouvez les événements de cette journée sur notre fil.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a63b34f6-e02e-11f1-8824-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T125840Z-625078051-RC2ONOA3SI00-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a63b34f6-e02e-11f1-8824-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T125840Z-625078051-RC2ONOA3SI00-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5da5c9c6-dff8-11f1-9718-aba0e2da7b6e</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 06:55:23 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a63b34f6-e02e-11f1-8824-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T125840Z-625078051-RC2ONOA3SI00-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© Benoît Tessier, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Projet de loi résilience : comment la France veut rattraper son retard en cybersécurité</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261113-projet-de-loi-r%C3%A9silience-comment-la-france-veut-rattraper-son-retard-en-cybers%C3%A9curit%C3%A9</link><description>
Alors que les cyberattaques se multiplient en France, l’Assemblée s'apprête à adopter, mardi, la loi résilience sur le renforcement de la cybersécurité. Retardé depuis deux ans, le texte multiplie par dix le nombre d’entités régulées et impose des sanctions financières en cas de manquement aux obligations de prévention, sans prévoir de financements supplémentaires.

L’utilisation de la loi suisse sur les banques contre les journalistes d’investigation pourrait constituer une menace contre la liberté de la presse.]]></description><guid isPermaLink="true">https://www.lemonde.fr/les-decodeurs/article/2026/11/16/en-suisse-l-inculpation-inedite-d-un-journaliste-via-la-loi-sur-les-banques-nourrit-des-inquietudes_6811403_4355770.html</guid><link>https://www.lemonde.fr/les-decodeurs/article/2026/11/16/en-suisse-l-inculpation-inedite-d-un-journaliste-via-la-loi-sur-les-banques-nourrit-des-inquietudes_6811403_4355770.html</link><media:content width="644" height="322" url="https://img.lemde.fr/2026/10/16/690/0/5184/2592/644/322/60/0/c452dcf_ftp-1-3otqrlh5xtx5-2026-10-16t114911z-1613644488-rc2a6s9i94bq-rtrmadp-3-swiss-press-freedom.JPG"><media:description type="plain">Le journaliste Lukas Hässig, à Zurich, le 25 janvier 2022.</media:description><media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">Arnd Wiegmann / REUTERS</media:credit></media:content></item></channel></rss>
